hints: Forget the median for a moment. Suppose you cut each series into a left part and a right part so that the two left parts together hold exactly half the readings. What would make that cut the right one?

Every reading on the left would have to be no larger than every reading on the right. Because each series is sorted, that is only two comparisons: the last of each left part against the first of the other right part.
Choosing how many readings to take from the first series fixes how many come from the second, so there is only one number to search - and the two comparisons say which way to move.
Search over the shorter series, and use infinities for the ends so that taking none or all of it needs no special case.
